story: Wisakedjak is a trickster spirit, known as the Crane Manitou, who appears in the storytelling traditions of northern peoples. He is a figure much like other trickster beings found among neighboring peoples, and his name takes many different forms depending on the language and community telling his story. As with many mythological figures of this kind, Wisakedjak's tales are used to explain how various animals came to be as they are, and how certain geographical features of the land came into existence. He is most often portrayed as the one responsible for bringing about a great flood that destroyed the entire world. In other versions of his story, Wisakedjak is also credited as one of the beings who took part in creating the world as it exists now, in the aftermath of that destruction. Some accounts say he accomplished this act of creation entirely on his own, relying on his own trickster power and cleverness. Other accounts say instead that he was given a special magic by the Creator, a higher power above him, specifically so that he could use it to remake the world after the flood had destroyed the old one. Thus Wisakedjak stands as both a destroyer, through the flood he caused, and a creator, through his role in rebuilding the world afterward, and his adventures continue to be told as explanations for the natural world as it now appears, including its animals and its landscapes.
